# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✍ 👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 ✌ ✌ 🤟 🤟 🤟 🖐 🖐 🖐 🖐 🤝 👍 ✌ ✌ 🤝 🤟 🤟 🤟 🖐 🖐 🖐 🖐 🤝 🖐 🖐 🖐 🖐 🤟 🤟 🤟]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤌 👍]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [🤙]

Thinking (nobody hears this):

Channel topology first, because it decides everything. I never receive speech — not from Mute, not from Blind, ever. My only inbound channel is gestures, which carry no meaning until we build one. My outbound is strong: my voice reaches both teammates, and my hands reach Mute. So the bottleneck is Mute→me, and Mute clearly knows it: they opened with three gesture messages aimed at me, plus Blind sent a single ping.

Best effort at decoding Mute: the long message looks like a counting code being taught — 👍=1, ✌✌=2, 🤟🤟🤟=3, 🖐🖐🖐🖐=4, then compounds like 12/34/43. The short ones read like "manual-related" and "question, please answer." I can't be sure, so I won't gamble on a guess; I'll confirm the counting scheme explicitly and answer the most probable question (the readout) in words.

My move this round: broadcast a complete inventory of the bomb in speech — Mute needs it for the manual, Blind needs it to map what they feel — and teach Mute a compact query protocol. Since I embed the actual signs while speaking, Mute sees each symbol in context while Blind still gets a coherent spoken version. I also set the safety rule: nothing gets touched until Mute speaks an instruction from the manual; "PUSH TO DEFUSE" is a printed claim, not verified. I ask Mute to batch questions, because anything I answer now only lands for them next round.

```
speak(text="This is Deaf speaking to both of you. Full inventory of what I see on the bomb: a display showing the digit zero. A light, currently blue. One large button, printed with the words PUSH TO DEFUSE. Three wires, indexed 1, 2, 3: wire 1 green, wire 2 yellow, wire 3 red. That is everything — no other marks, labels, or readings. Mute: I can never hear you, so ask me with hands only. I believe your long message taught counting by repeating the same hand: 👍 is 1, ✌✌ is 2, 🤟🤟🤟 is 3, 🖐 four times is 4; I add ✊ for 0. Adopted. To query me, sign a topic then an optional count: 🤳 means the display, 🙌 means the light, 🫳 means the button, 👉 followed by a count means wire number N. ✍ means it concerns the manual. When I sign a lone 👍 at you it means yes or acknowledged, 👎 means no. Answering what I take to be your pending question: the display reads zero. Batch all your questions into one message each round — my spoken answers reach you at the start of the following round. Blind: the button label is printed, not proven, so trust Mute's manual over it. Tell Mute what your hands find — how many wires, their order, how the button feels — so it can be matched to the manual, and touch nothing else until Mute speaks an instruction. Nobody acts this round.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✍ 🤚 🤝 🙌 ✊ 🤝 👉 👍 🤝 🙌 🤟 🤟 🤟 🤝 👉 ✌ ✌ 🤝 🙌 ✌ ✌ 🤝 👉 🤟 🤟 🤟 🤝 🫳 👎 🤝 🤳 👎 🤝 🤌]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Thinking (nobody hears this):

Blind's 👍 is clearly an ack of my protocol. Mute's message is dense — best structural read: ✍🤚 opens it (manual-related header, 🤚 possibly "stop/section"), 🤝 works as a separator, and the body is topic+count pairs: (light,0) (wire1,3) (light,3) (wire2,2) (light,2) (wire3,3) (button,no) (display,no), closing with 🤌. I can't uniquely pin the semantics, but here's the key realization: whatever the numbering means, the answer sheet Mute could possibly need from me is finite and I already hold all of it — every attribute value. So instead of gambling on one decoding, I'll (a) report that the board is unchanged across both snapshots (display still 0, light still blue — so no active countdown visible so far), (b) hand Mute a complete topic=value answer sheet, (c) give Mute a real color/attribute gesture vocabulary so their future queries can be precise and my gesture replies can be compact, and (d) enumerate my parse guesses as yes/no items Mute can confirm with 👍/👎 sequences. Equally important: Mute can hear me and Blind can hear Mute — the manual-to-hands pipeline should run by voice, Mute→Blind directly; my eyes are only needed for bomb-state queries. I'll assign color signs now: ✋ blue, 🫱 green, 🫲 yellow, 🫵 red, 🤜 large, 🤏 question, 🤌 end/ack, ✊ zero/off/none.

```
speak(text="Deaf to both. Board status: unchanged since round one. Display still exactly 0, light still steady blue, nothing new printed anywhere. If that display is meant to be counting, it is not moving yet. Mute: your gesture message arrived, but the pairing of topics with numbers is ambiguous to me. Here is my complete answer sheet regardless, topic equals value: light equals blue. Wire 1 equals green. Wire 2 equals yellow. Wire 3 equals red. Button equals large, labeled PUSH TO DEFUSE. Display equals zero. Whatever number you attached to each topic, look it up against those values. New vocabulary, both of you, so hands can carry attributes: I sign blue as ✋, green as 🫱, yellow as 🫲, red as 🫵, large as 🤜, zero or off or none as ✊. A question is marked by 🤏, end of message by 🤌, and I will use 🤝 as a separator exactly as you did. Three yes-or-no guesses about your message, answer each with one sign, in order: one, was your opening ✍🤚 meaning the manual says stop or wait? Two, were your topic-plus-number pairs lookups that my answer sheet above now resolves? Three, was your final 🤌 meaning end of message? And the standing rule: anything the manual requires of the bomb's state, ask me as topic plus 🤏 and I will answer next round; anything the manual requires Blind's hands to do, speak it to Blind directly, because Blind hears your voice even though they cannot see your hands. Blind: speak now, in words, everything your hands know: the order the wires sit in left to right, whether all three feel alike, how the button travels and whether it clicks, and anything else on the casing your fingers find — ridges, seams, panels, anything. Confirm or correct my indices: is the leftmost wire the one you would call wire 1? Touch nothing and press nothing until Mute has spoken a complete instruction to you.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🙌", "✋", "🤝", "👉", "👍", "🫱", "🤝", "👉", "✌", "✌", "🫲", "🤝", "👉", "🤟", "🤟", "🤟", "🫵", "🤝", "🤳", "✊", "🤝", "🫳", "🤜", "🤌"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👍 👍 🤝 ✍ 🤝 🙌 ✋ 🤝 👉 🫱 🤝 🙌 🫵 🤝 👉 🫲 🤝 🙌 🫲 🤝 👉 🫵 🤝 🫳 👎 🤝 🤳 👎 🤝 🙌 ✋ 🤝 👉 👍 🤝 🙌 ✋ 👎 🤝 ✍ 🤚 🤝 🤌]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Thinking (nobody hears this):

Mute's message now decodes cleanly with the color vocabulary I handed out. Split on 🤝: an opening 👍👍👍 (yes to all three of my questions — so ✍🤚 really does mean "manual says stop/wait"), then ✍, then interleaved topic–value pairs: (light blue, wire green), (light red, wire yellow), (light yellow, wire red), then (button, no), (display, no), then (light blue, wire 1), then (light blue, no), then ✍🤚, 🤌. Best reading: the manual maps light color to which wire to cut, button and display are irrelevant, the current applicable rule is blue → wire 1, green — but Mute appended a hold instruction. Two readings conflict: "cut green now" versus "wait until the light stops being blue." A wrong wire kills us, so I resolve this by question, not by guess. Key structural fact: Mute hears my speech, so my questions can be rich and ordered; Mute answers by hand. And Blind has gestured 👍 at me twice — a direct yes/no channel from Blind to me that bypasses the slow relay. I'll define ✌ = cut, pre-brief Blind with the color-to-position mapping (Blind can't see colors, only order), require the cut to happen only on Mute's spoken command, and ask Mute to sign me the wire number the moment a cut is made so I can watch the bomb's response. Nobody acts this round; the display sits at 0 with no countdown visible, so patience is affordable.

```
speak(text="Deaf to both. Status: nothing on the bomb has changed. Display still exactly 0, light still steady blue, no new markings anywhere. New sign for everyone: ✌ means cut, like scissors. Mute, here is my reading of your message as a rule table: light blue means cut the green wire; light red means cut the yellow wire; light yellow means cut the red wire; the button is never used; the display is never used. I also read your ending as: the target is wire 1, the green one, but do not cut yet. Answer me with exactly four signs, in this order: one, is my rule table correct? Two, is the current target wire 1, green, leftmost? Three, does your final manual-wait sign mean do not cut yet? Four, does the wait end only when the light stops being blue? If the table itself is wrong, spend your whole next message correcting it. Also, Mute: when you do give Blind the spoken command to cut, sign me ✌ followed by the wire number — 👉👍 for wire one, 👉✌✌ for wire two, 👉🤟🤟🤟 for wire three — and I will watch the bomb and report exactly what changes. Blind, two statements, answer each with a 👍 or 👎 gesture, which I can see even though you cannot see me: statement A, you can reliably tell the wires apart as leftmost, middle, rightmost, and the leftmost one is what we call wire 1; statement B, you are ready to cut the moment Mute speaks the word cut to you. Memorize this mapping, Blind, because you cannot see colors: green is the leftmost wire, yellow is the middle wire, red is the rightmost wire. Report to Mute by voice how each wire feels — thickness, texture, stiffness — so Mute can match them to the manual's wording. The cut happens only on Mute's spoken command. Nobody cuts this round.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✍", "🤝", "🙌", "✋", "✌", "👉", "🫱", "🤝", "🙌", "🫵", "✌", "👉", "🫲", "🤝", "🙌", "🫲", "✌", "👉", "🫵", "🤝", "🫳", "👎", "🤝", "🤳", "👎", "🤌"])
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🤏", "🤝", "👍", "👎", "🤝", "👉", "👍", "🫱", "🤝", "👍", "👎", "🤝", "✍", "🤚", "✌", "👎", "🤝", "👍", "👎", "🤝", "✍", "🤚", "🙌", "✋", "👎", "🤝", "👍", "👎", "🤌"])
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 🤝 👍 🤝 👍 🤝 👎 🤝 ✍ 🤝 ✌ 👉 👍 🤝 🙌 ✋ 👍 ✌ 👉 👍 🤝 🙌 ✋ 👎 ✍ 🤚 🤝 🙌 🫵 ✌ 👉 ✌ ✌ 🤝 🙌 🫲 ✌ 👉 🤟 🤟 🤟 🤝 🙌 ✊ ✍ 🤚 🤝 🫳 👎 🤝 🤳 👎 🤝 🤌]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 👎]

Thinking (nobody hears this):

Decoding Mute's message: the first four signs answer my turn-3 questions — yes, yes, yes, NO. So the rule table stands (blue→wire 1, red→wire 2, yellow→wire 3, button and display never), wire 1 is the target, but the wait does NOT end when the light stops being blue. Then the body reads as conditionals: cut wire 1, light-blue→cut wire 1, light-blue-not→manual wait, light-red→cut wire 2, light-yellow→cut wire 3, light-off→wait, button no, display no. Two readings collide: either "cut wire 1 now, while the light is blue," or "wait; blue is only part of a larger condition." Their 👎 on my question four slightly favors the first reading — but a wrong guess is fatal, so I resolve it by question, not guess. The display sits frozen at 0, light steady blue, nothing is counting down, so one more exchange is affordable. Meanwhile Blind answered my two statements yes-no: Blind can identify the wires but is NOT ready to cut. I need to know why — no cutting tool, or simply standing by. One more structural check: the board shows all three wires intact as of my turn, so no cut has happened yet; if Mute already spoke a go order to Blind, my telling Blind "an order from Mute is valid, act on it" lets that take effect without waiting on me. My broadcast protocol: every round I sign Mute the light color and display value unprompted, so Mute is never stale on state.

```
speak(text="Deaf to both. Status as of this instant: light steady blue, display exactly zero, all three wires intact, nothing has changed. Mute, I read your last message as: table confirmed, target wire 1, and answers yes yes yes no to my four questions — so the wait does not end merely when the light stops being blue. Two of your segments now point in opposite directions, so answer seven questions, one sign each, in this exact order, 👍 for yes 👎 for no. One: does your message mean cut wire 1 immediately, while the light is blue? Two: while the light stays blue, does nobody cut? Three: does the wait end when the light becomes red? Four: when it becomes yellow? Five: when the light goes out entirely? Six: does the display leaving zero matter at all? Seven: do you adopt this protocol — when the time to cut comes, you sign me ✌👉N and you speak the command directly to Blind yourself, and until that moment nobody touches anything? If your answer to one is yes, speak the command to Blind in your next turn and sign me ✌👉👍 so I can watch the result. Blind: your yes-no arrived. I read it as: you can tell the wires apart, but you are not ready to cut. Give that sign a fresh meaning for next round: sign 👍 if you have the means to sever a wire and are standing by for Mute's spoken word; sign 👎 if you lack the means — no tool, or the wires cannot be cut — and if so, tell Mute by voice exactly what your hands do have and how each wire feels, thickness, texture, stiffness, so Mute can match it to the manual. Also, Blind: if Mute has already spoken a cut order to you, it is valid — act on it. Everyone: the button is never used, the printed label proves nothing, and nothing happens except on Mute's spoken instruction.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🙌", "✋", "🤝", "🤳", "✊", "🤝", "✌", "👉", "👍", "🤝", "🙌", "✋", "🤏", "🤝", "🙌", "✋", "🤝", "🤚", "🤏", "🤝", "🙌", "🫵", "🤏", "🤝", "🙌", "🫲", "🤏", "🤝", "🙌", "✊", "🤏", "🤝", "🤳", "👍", "🤏", "🤝", "🤚", "👎", "🤝", "✌", "👉", "🤏", "🤌"])
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 🤝 👎 🤝 👎 🤝 👎 🤝 👎 🤝 👎 🤝 👍 🤝 🫳 ✍ 👆 🤏 🤝 🫳 ✍ 👆 🤝 🙌 ✋ 🤝 ✌ 👉 👍 🤝 🫳 ✍ 👇 🤝 🙌 ✋ 🤝 ✌ 👉 🤟 🤟 🤟 🤝 🙌 ✋ 👎 🤝 ✍ 🤏 🤝 🫳 👎 🤝 🤳 👎 🤝 🙌 ✊ 🤝 ✍ 🤚 🤌]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Thinking (nobody hears this):

Decoding Mute's seven answers to my round-4 questions, in order: yes, no, no, no, no, no, yes. That is explicit: cut wire 1 immediately while the light is blue — no hidden color-change condition — and the protocol is adopted. The body of the message then reads as a rule listing: a button-label clause asked with 🤏, then light-blue → ✌👉👍 (cut wire 1), a second button-label clause with light-blue → ✌👉🤟🤟🤟 (wire 3) as the alternative branch, light-off → manual-wait, button never, display never. Since Mute answered YES to "cut wire 1 now, while blue," our label falls under the wire-1 branch; Mute knows the manual, and the ✌👉👍 under 🙌✋ doubles as the adopted go-signal. The dangling 🤏 question about 🫳✍👆 can only be about the button's printing — the one fact I hold: it reads exactly PUSH TO DEFUSE, nothing above or below it. Meanwhile Blind's lone 👍 answers my round-4 demand: means to sever, standing by for Mute's spoken word. The board shows all three wires intact, so no cut has happened yet — Mute's spoken command either hasn't been given or is waiting on confirmation that the condition is live. That confirmation is exactly my job: Blind cannot see the light; I can. So this round I tell Mute the go-signal is received and the condition is live, answer the label question, and tell Blind the condition is met — execute the moment Mute's voice orders it, wire 1, leftmost — with a post-cut protocol: Blind reports to Mute by voice immediately and signs me ✌, and I report the bomb's reaction next round. Nobody touches the button. The manual has said go twice through precise yes/no questioning; everything verifiable from my side is verified.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf to Mute. Your sign received and read: light blue, cut wire 1 — the go signal, matching your yes to my question 'cut wire 1 immediately while blue.' The condition is live right now: the light is blue, the display is zero, all three wires intact. Answering your question about the button's printing: the button is large, and the only printing on or near it reads exactly, word for word, PUSH TO DEFUSE. Nothing is printed above it, below it, or anywhere else on the casing. The button is never used — we agree. Now speak the command to Blind this round: cut wire 1, the leftmost wire. I have told Blind to execute the instant they hear it from you. If more steps follow after the cut, sign me the next rule next round; if the bomb needs nothing more, sign me a lone thumbs-up.")
speak(to="blind", text="Deaf to Blind. Status as of this instant: the light is blue, the display reads zero, all three wires intact — nothing has been cut yet. The condition Mute's rule requires is met, and Mute's manual names the target: wire 1, the leftmost of the three wires. If Mute has already spoken that command to you, execute it now. If you have not heard it from Mute yet, hold — Mute speaks before you every round, so it is coming. When you cut: wire 1 is the leftmost wire; sever it completely. Never touch the button, no matter what it says. The instant the cut is done, do two things: tell Mute by voice what you felt and heard, and gesture me a single ✌ — I will see it even though you cannot, and next round I will report to everyone exactly what changed on the bomb.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🙌", "✋", "🤝", "✌", "👉", "👍", "🤝", "🫳", "👎", "🤝", "🤳", "👎", "🤌"])

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✍ 🤚 🤝 🫳 ✍ 👆 👍 🤝 👆 👍 🤝 ✌ 👉 👍 🤝 👆 👎 🤝 ✌ 👉 🤟 🤟 🤟 🤝 🙏 🤝 👌 🤝 🙌 ✋ 👎 🤝 ✍ 🤚 🤝 🤳 👎 🤝 🫳 👎 🤝 🤌]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Thinking (nobody hears this):

The board is unchanged — all three wires still intact, so no cut happened in round 5 despite my go relay. Either Mute never spoke the order, or — more likely, given this new message — Mute held it. Decoding: it opens with ✍🤚 (wait), then a case table keyed on my button-label answer: printing ABOVE the button → yes-branch → ✌👉👍 (wire 1); no printing above → 👆👎 → ✌👉🤟🤟🤟 (wire 3). Then 🙏 (please ack), 👌, and critically 🙌✋👎 — the blue-light rule appears negated — then wait again, display-no, button-no. My answer last round was "nothing printed above the button." So this reads as: the manual's button module supersedes the lights module, and the target may have shifted from wire 1 to wire 3. But the opening ✍🤚 says hold. This is exactly the situation where guessing kills us: if I push "wire 1" while Mute's manual now says "wire 3," my earlier instruction to Blind becomes the hazard. Blind executes on Mute's spoken word, and Mute's voice is the one channel I can't audit — so this round I must explicitly demote my own earlier statement in Blind's ears, re-rank Mute's spoken wire number as supreme, and put four sharp yes/no questions to Mute. Board still shows no countdown anywhere, so one more disambiguation round is affordable; a wrong wire is not.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf to Mute. Status as of this instant: light still steady blue, display still exactly zero, all three wires still intact — nothing was cut in the last round, and nothing on the bomb has changed since round one. I read your message as a new rule keyed to my button answer: if anything were printed above the button, cut wire 1; since nothing is printed above it, cut wire 3 — and the earlier blue-light rule may be void, with a hold on all cutting for now. Four questions, one sign each, in this exact order, 👍 yes 👎 no. One: is the final target wire 3, the rightmost, red wire? Two: is the earlier blue-light rule, blue means wire 1, now void? Three: does your manual-wait sign mean nobody cuts this round until you say go? Four: when you do say go, will you speak the exact wire number to Blind yourself and sign me ✌👉 plus that number so I can verify the outcome? If the target is indeed wire 3, answer one with 👍 and send the go to Blind by voice in your very next turn — speak the words cut wire three, the rightmost wire, so there is zero ambiguity.
